raw_response:
I will do cotton the way I know works here, not too fancy, not too risky. Last year I also planted cotton, and on my small 4.5 mu I cannot gamble. If the fertilizer is too little, the bolls will be small and sparse, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. I usually watch the men around me who get steady harvests, and most of us put the base fertilizer on first, then add some nitrogen later when the plants start growing strong. I have well water, so I will not let the field stay dry at the key times. I do most of the work myself with one family helper, so I will keep the field management simple: plough first, use improved seed, feed the crop enough, water several times, and spray when insects show up. On 4.5 mu, every bag costs money, so I will not pile on too much, but I will still put enough to protect yield.
